title: Koopman neural-operator regime views on a periodic advection-diffusion family
hypothesis: One shared Fourier-latent Koopman operator parameterized by a scalar system code recovers heldout PDE regimes with lower complete bytes than per-regime FNO kernels, while preserving field quality and spectral stability.
task: periodic 1D advection-diffusion semigroup at a fixed horizon, varying diffusivity kappa

fresh.release_rule: No fresh access after exact native parameter-conditioning alias or a frozen quality/storage gate miss.

controls: independent per-regime FNO Fourier multiplier tables
Mirror scalar diffusivity code over shared Fourier generator
native conditional Fourier/KNO parameterization implementing the same physical law

paid: independent multiplier tables for FNO control

pass_gate: Heldout field nRMSE <=0.02, max multiplier magnitude <=1, at least 25% fewer bytes than independent FNO tables, and strict frontier gain over native conditional Fourier/KNO control.
fail_gate: FAIL Mirror-specific value for exact native control alias, quality/stability miss, insufficient bytes savings, or no native-control frontier gain.

compute.active_compute: rFFT/irFFT plus one complex multiplier per retained mode; report per-regime exponential code construction separately
compute.wall_time: small CPU transform calibration; no neural-network/GPU throughput claim

boundaries: Known linear PDE semigroup in a known Fourier basis; no trained KNO, FNO, or nonlinear PDE claim.
The scalar diffusivity is supplied and charged; no PDE-parameter inference claim.
Native conditional Fourier law is intentionally a strong control and may exactly match the Mirror view.
This is a mechanism/storage screen for the operator insertion point, not reproduction of the cited KNO architecture.
